HOMELESS SERVICES ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, APRIL 2, 2025
  1500 HUGHES WAY STE. C-300 LONG BEACH, CA 90810
  HOUSING AUTHORITY, 4:30 PM

Julie Lie, Chair  James Howat, Member
Kimberly Lewis, Vice Chair  Doug Killion,
Sarah Bedy, Member  Member
Pam Chotiswatdi, Member  Angela Russell, Member
Laurence Hilliard, Member  Patricia Scott, Member
  Stephen Wood, Member

  FINISHED AGENDA & MINUTES

CALL TO ORDER

Chair Julie Lie, called the meeting to order at 4:35 PM.

ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present: Bedy, Chotiswatdi, Howat, Lewis, Lie, Wood, Killion, Russell, Scott,
  Hilliard

Also present: Stephanie Sosa, Community Program Specialist, Jennifer Santana, Community
Program Specialist, Paul Duncan, Homeless Services Bureau Manager.

Chair Julie Lie Presiding

REGULAR AGENDA

1.  25-54749  Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Homeless Services Advisory
  Committee meeting of Wednesday, March 5, 2025.

  A motion was made by Member Bedy, seconded by Member Lewis, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  6  Scott, Russell, Killion, Lie, Lewis, Bedy
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 4  Hilliard, Wood, Howat, Chotiswatdi

  • Cheri Weeks Chief operating officer at First to Serve provided an overview of
  the nonprofit organization. The nonprofit that was founded in 2002, dedicated
  to addressing homelessness, substance abuse, mental illness and domestic
  violence.
  • First to Serve operates three shelters in the city of Long Beach and one

  Page 1 of 5
   HOMELESS SERVICES ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, APRIL 2, 2025
  1500 HUGHES WAY STE. C-300 LONG BEACH, CA 90810
  HOUSING AUTHORITY, 4:30 PM

  winter shelter site.
  • Transitional housing is provided for individuals and families, with specialized
  programs for men, women and children.
  • Cheri discussed ways that the city and residents can help provide support,
  including support to reduce stigma against people experiencing
  homelessness.
  • First to Serve is looking to grow their clinical department in the upcoming
  years.
  • Committee members raised concerns about the capacity at the facilities, and
  Cheri responded to their questions, providing the necessary information.

2.  25-54752  Recommendation to receive and file the First to Serve Interim Shelter Operations
  Overview presentation.

  A motion was made by Member Lewis, seconded by Voting Member Russell,
  to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  6  Scott, Russell, Killion, Lie, Lewis, Bedy
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 4  Hilliard, Wood, Howat, Chotiswatdi

3.  25-54750  Recommendation to receive and file updates from the Mayor’s Fund and the
  Continuum of Care (CoC) HSAC representative.

  A motion was made by Member Bedy, seconded by Voting Member Killion, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  6  Scott, Russell, Killion, Lie, Lewis, Bedy
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 4  Hilliard, Wood, Howat, Chotiswatdi

  Mayor’s Fund Subcommittee
  • City Staff Stephanie Sosa provided updates on the Mayor’s Fund balance,
  as of January 2025 the ending balance is $155.080.71. Current agencies
  awarded are spending down their funds and the total contributions awarded
  in January 2025 was $ 2,070.69.
  • Vice Chair Lewis, provided updates regarding the SOP, the subcommittee is
  working on finalizing verbiage to the document.
  CoC Representative Updates

  Page 2 of 5
   HOMELESS SERVICES ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, APRIL 2, 2025
  1500 HUGHES WAY STE. C-300 LONG BEACH, CA 90810
  HOUSING AUTHORITY, 4:30 PM

  • Vice Chair Lewis provided updates for the LB CoC Board meeting in March.
  The board met to discuss policy changes and focus on ESG RUSH in
  response to the fires.

4.  25-54751  Recommendation to receive and file updates from the Policy Subcommittee
  representative.

  A motion was made by Member Lewis, seconded by Voting Member Killion, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  7  Scott, Russell, Killion, Lie, Lewis, Howat, Bedy
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 3  Hilliard, Wood, Chotiswatdi

  • Member Bedy provided an update on the Policy subcommittee meeting held
  in March.
  • The subcommittee is working on updating the 2025 Policy Recommendation
  which include a pilot program for trash removal, portable restrooms and
  hygiene services. Once finalized the subcommittee will bring the
  recommendations to the HSAC meeting for a vote.
  • A member of the public commented on the recommendation regarding public
  restrooms.
  • Member Scott agreed with the public comment, if encampments are being
  cleaned out there will be no one to service in those areas.
  • Members of the committee discussed how to bring recommendations
  forward as a committee.
  • Member Howat joins the meeting at 5:05 p.m.
  • Committee members would like to have future discussion on the developing
  recommendations as a committee.

5.  25-54754  Recommendation to receive and file a discussion on the Homeless Services
  Advisory Committee Annual report.

  A motion was made by Voting Member Killion, seconded by Member Lewis, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  7  Scott, Russell, Killion, Lie, Lewis, Howat, Bedy
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None

  Page 3 of 5
   HOMELESS SERVICES ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, APRIL 2, 2025
  1500 HUGHES WAY STE. C-300 LONG BEACH, CA 90810
  HOUSING AUTHORITY, 4:30 PM

  Absent:  3 Hilliard, Wood, Chotiswatdi

  • Chair Julie Lie advised the committee that HSAC should resume the practice
  of producing annual reports, noting that these reports previously included
  policy recommendations
  • Committee members discussed whether the development of the report
  should be directed to the Policy Subcommittee or handled through an ad hoc
  meeting that would allow for collaboration between staff and committee
  members.
  • A member of the public provided feedback, highly recommending that HSAC
  does do an annual report and include the Mayor’s Fund.

6.  25-54753  Recommendation to receive and file the Homeless Services Bureau Staff
  Operations and Updates Report by Paul Duncan from the Health Department.

  A motion was made by Voting Member Killion, seconded by Member Bedy, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  7  Scott, Russell, Killion, Lie, Lewis, Howat, Bedy
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 3  Hilliard, Wood, Chotiswatdi

  • Bureau Manager Paul Duncan gave a presentation to the committee,
  providing an overview of the Bureau’s organizational chart.
  • The LA County Board of Supervisors has voted to pull funding from LAHSA.
  The county will shift the funds towards creating a new countywide
  department to manage the crisis.
  • The city of Long Beach currently has one contract with LAHSA that is being
  monitored.
  • New funds under Measure A allocations there is $10M set aside CoC’s, the
  city of Long Beach anticipates receiving $8.5M.
  • Staff along with the Mayor, City Prosecutor and Chief of Police presented at
  the Annual Neighborhood Leadership conference, focused on the City’s
  response to unsheltered homelessness.
  • Encampment resolution round 2 data has been provided to the LB Post for a
  story. Staff is working on ensuring successful matches to PHK-Former Best
  western.
  • The Youth Navigation Center construction has been completed. Both the
  navigation center and PHK-Best Western are waiting on furniture and
  fixtures to be complete. PHK-Luxury Inn has multiple construction delays
  with additional work added, estimated completion date is

  Page 4 of 5
   HOMELESS SERVICES ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, APRIL 2, 2025
  1500 HUGHES WAY STE. C-300 LONG BEACH, CA 90810
  HOUSING AUTHORITY, 4:30 PM

  August/September.
  • Members of the committee had questions regarding the Youth navigation
  center, Measure A and tiny homes. Staff responded to the questions asked.
  • HUD is facing a 85% staff reductions, this is the department that works on
  executing our contracts and payments for CoC, ESG and HOME funds.
  Potential loss of Emergency Housing Voucher program, of which Long
  Beach received 582 vouchers.

7.  25-54756  Recommendation to receive and file future HSAC agenda items.

  A motion was made by Member Howat, seconded by Member Lewis, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  7  Scott, Russell, Killion, Lie, Lewis, Howat, Bedy
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 3  Hilliard, Wood, Chotiswatdi

  • There will be a presentation by the City Attorney’s Office focused on the
  Brown Act and Robert’s Rules of Order.

PUBLIC COMMENT

  • No public comment.

ANNOUNCEMENTS

  • The next Long Beach CoC General Meeting in May will be at Cabrillo villages
  • St Lukes community garden 3 yr anniversary reception on May 3rd.

ADJOURNMENT

Chair Julie Lie, adjourns the meeting at 6:18 p.m.
